issues.detail: The new .. deprecated:: directive reads 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`'. All three reviewers flagged this. Specifications are part of the program, and a misspelled reference to the replacement API is a small but easy spec defect to fix while the directive is being added.

issues.description: Deprecation test does not exercise the stderr redirect path.
issues.detail: test_deprecated_redirected only asserts the stdout substitution. Since the deprecation message promises equivalence with both contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr, a symmetric assertion on stderr=output would round out the contract test for the full surface being deprecated until 5.0.

issues.description: Deprecation note should clarify that stdout+stderr requires nesting two contextlib managers.
issues.detail: contextlib.redirect_stderr is a separate context manager from redirect_stdout, so callers of the deprecated redirected() that pass both streams must nest two contexts to preserve the original postcondition. Worth a sentence in the migration note so substitutability is unambiguous.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts this PR as a clean, well-scoped deprecation of falcon.testing.redirected in favor of contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr. The wrapper is contract-preserving (streams restored on exit, including on exception), substitutability holds, and complexity is unchanged. The only consensus findings are minor polish items: a 'stlib'/'stdlib' typo in the new docstring directive, a test that exercises only the stdout path, and a migration note that could mention nesting two contextlib managers when both streams are redirected. No correctness, performance, or LSP concerns.
